1	# Terminology research pass: shared brief
2	
3	You run ONE terminology pass for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook (`/home/user/guidebook`) for the language-and-jurisdiction pair your instruction names. It is part of a wave over the P1+P2+P3 languages. Pilot passes already exist (`terminology-pass/FR-FR/`, and DE-DE and JA-JP if finished); read `FR-FR/pass-record.md` and look at its `build.py`, which you may copy and adapt as your verifier.
4	
5	Read `CLAUDE.md` first (rules 0, 5, 7a, 8, 10; section 5 failure modes; section 7 traps incl. the Wayback route), and the three entries headed "Owner statements 2026-11-06" and the fourth in `references/project-standards.md`.
6	
7	## What this is and is not
8	- The English register is the SEARCH PLAN, not the vocabulary, and it is Canadian English from one rating instrument (RHFAC), digested in `rhfac-b651-catalogue.md` (sections 2 to 6), `rhfac-criteria.tsv` (640 criteria) and `b651-headings.tsv` (the CSA/ASC B651:23 clause structure). It is a guideline, not definitive.
9	- Rendering the register into your language produces FLAGGED, MODEL-GENERATED SEARCH SEEDS (owner OR-12b: terms you believe are IN USE in that jurisdiction, never word for word). Seeds point the reading and are never findings, never aliases, never vocabulary.
10	- A FINDING is a phrase VERBATIM in a retrieved text of that jurisdiction in its own language, with locator and a quote that verifies in the saved bytes.
11	- The register must not end where English ends: read the instrument IN FULL in its own language and record every design quantity, element, technique and defined category it treats, including ones the register lacks (reverse harvest; owner E1: a concept first met outside English is named by the instrument's own phrase, never an English gloss).
12	- Terminology only: do not extract values as findings.
13	
14	## Concept list
15	Use the 32 concepts recurring in three or more sections (catalogue 2.1), the quantity-bearing words (2.2), the base's active parameters (`select p.parameter_id, t.canonical_en from base_parameters p join terms t using(term_id)`), and the B651 clause headings that RHFAC does not name (`b651-headings.tsv`, last column). Existing aliases in your language (`select alias, alias_type, jurisdiction, notes from term_aliases where lower(language)='<code>'`) are MODEL-GENERATED SEEDS, never findings.
16	
17	## Lessons from the French pilot (apply them)
18	1. A text match is not a sense match. Record FOUND only where the instrument uses the phrase in the register concept's sense; say so in the note. "inclinaison" appearing in an unrelated sense is not a finding.
19	2. The register is criterion-shaped: near-duplicate rows share observations. Count distinct phrases as well as observations, and do not let near-duplicates inflate FOUND.
20	3. The instrument may split or merge concepts differently (the French fixed ramp is a different word from "rampe"; its corridor is not "couloir"). Record the carve difference; do not force a one-to-one map.
21	4. The drafting structure itself may differ (aim then prescription, defined categories, equivalent-effect routes). Note it in the pass record.
22	5. Held aliases that are word-for-word translations and occur in no instrument should be reported as such.
23	6. Instrument lists cannot be derived from the base for most pairs. Say how you built yours and what you could not derive.
24	
25	## Procedure
26	1. **Instruments.** Primary accessibility instruments for buildings in force, current editions only, free official texts first (the national law and regulation portal, the building authority's published code). Derive candidates from `research_code_leads`, `references/standards-registry.md` and `select ref_id, pub_title, standard_number from evidence_sources where jurisdiction='<J>'`, then search. A paywalled standard you cannot retrieve is NOT-OBTAINABLE: log the attempt; do not substitute memory of its content.
27	2. **Retrieve and persist** from the repository ROOT (retrieval_log writes relative to cwd; running it elsewhere misplaces artefacts):
28	   `cd /home/user/guidebook && python3 - <<'PY'` / `import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/research'); import retrieval_log as r; r.fetch(URL, session='session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review', purpose='terminology pass <PAIR>: <what>')` / `PY`.
29	   fetch() returns None for non-JSON but persists the bytes and a manifest line under `retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/`. A publisher block or a JavaScript shell: use the Wayback `if_` route (CLAUDE.md section 7), as the French pass did for Légifrance. Extract text with `pdftotext -layout` or by stripping tags; save the text to `terminology-pass/<PAIR>/text/<artefact-sha-prefix>.txt` and record its sha256. Never disable TLS verification or unset the proxy. The owner has ruled that retrieved standards may be held in the repository.
30	3. **Read each retrieved instrument in full**, in its own language. Locate with scripts, read the located passages yourself, and record honestly what you read and what you did not [SKIPPED: part, why]. Image-only diagrams are unread.
31	4. **Record** under `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/terminology-pass/<PAIR>/` (PAIR like `DA-DK`):
32	   - `search-log.md`: every query verbatim, a prior expectation written BEFORE the result, the result, and a note on query shape (R14). Keep empties.
33	   - `instruments.tsv`: title as written, issuing body, edition in force, URL, sha256 of retrieved bytes, retrieval status, read in full yes/no/partly with what was skipped.
34	   - `observations.tsv`: concept (register label or REVERSE-HARVEST), phrase VERBATIM, language, instrument, locator, context quote verbatim, text file, quote_verified_in_text, note (ours).
35	   - `coverage.tsv`: one row per register concept: FOUND / FOUND-PARTIAL / SEARCHED-ABSENT (instrument read in full, concept not treated) / NOT-OBTAINABLE / NOT-READ, with a note.
36	   - `reverse-harvest.tsv`: what the instrument treats that no register row names, in its own phrase; any gloss clearly marked as ours.
37	   - `seeds.tsv`: model-generated seeds for register concepts NOT found, flagged MODEL-GENERATED, with the jurisdiction they are meant to be in use in. Short.
38	   - `build.py` (adapted from the French pass) that regenerates the TSVs and exits 1 on any quote not found verbatim in the saved text.
39	   - `pass-record.md` (verdict first, at most 80 lines): retrieved and read, not read and why, counts by script (command beside each), where this language's instrument carves the field differently from English, method defects, and a self-attack of the five likeliest ways the record is wrong.
40	5. **Hard prohibitions.** Do not write `data/guidebook.db` or run any `db.py` write verb or migration. Do not commit or push. Do not edit `CLAUDE.md` or any file outside your `terminology-pass/<PAIR>/` folder and `retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/`. Invent no citation, article number, URL or quotation; every locator and quote must come from bytes you retrieved. Use no pre-reset item codes (a letter, a hyphen, two digits). Do not use the French RHFAC edition. Canadian English in your own prose; objective tone, no flattery.
41	
42	Budget: depth on the one or two principal instruments over breadth. Stop when they are read in full and recorded, or when an unavoidable block is logged. Reply in at most 12 lines: verdict, instruments read in full vs not, counts (FOUND / FOUND-PARTIAL / ABSENT / REVERSE-HARVEST), the two most surprising carve differences with English, method defects, and the folder path.

## Owner rulings 2026-11-06 — minimise code; no net-negative requirement

Given in this session (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMkXnQsEwzR9oaTqn1), in three messages after the gap register for the two pipeline batches was filed and handed to an analyst, and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Each is quoted verbatim, including its lower case:

- (question) "net negative rule? that is supposed to be reserved for minimizing code infrastructure?"
- "we want to MINIMIZE code wherever possible. we don't require a net negative because the extreme of that means we end up with no code"
- "we want the bare essentials in the most code efficient manner possible so that we are agile and lean"

**What this does.** The readings are the assistant's and are marked; the owner's words above are the ruling.

1. **The standing constraint is minimal code, not a shrinking total.** The 2026-10-12 direction (as little code as possible) stands and is sharpened to the bare essentials written as efficiently as possible. The net-negative requirement that operationalised it (a PR touching `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/` or `skills/` may not raise their line total without naming the exception) is not required. [ASSUMPTION: the net-negative bullet is read as a rule about code infrastructure only, as the owner's question puts it, so it never applied to research rows, owner decisions, doctrine or prose.]
2. **What stays.** The tests of `CLAUDE.md` section 8 that need no count: before adding a check, script or table, state what wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it; nothing is added without naming what reads it. [ASSUMPTION: "wherever possible" is a standing preference weighed case by case, not a gate, so a defect that reaches the guidebook is still fixed with the smallest code that closes it.]
3. **Supersession.** The net-negative bullet of `CLAUDE.md` section 8 is rewritten in place, as that file's own rule directs (fix the sentence, put the account in the commit message). No `SUPERSEDES` pair is written for it: the audit anchors on a target quote that must still occur once, and the sentence it would quote no longer exists. The simplification plan's W3 (`workplan/2026-10-12-simplification-workplan.md`) and the "net-negative" item of the standing constraints and W1-W10 list in `workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md` restate the old bullet; they are plans, left as written, and this ruling governs where they differ.

**What is unblocked, and what still waits.** Nothing waits on the owner. The Opus resolution analysis of GAP-074 to GAP-096 was told of the ruling and is to classify each tooling recommendation as close-as-accepted, rule or prose, reuse, delete or new code.

CONDITION: any session writing or reviewing a PR that touches `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/` or `skills/`, or asked whether a change must reduce the line total.
ACTION: (1) Do not require or claim a net-negative total. Name what the added code reads and what wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it, and name any code it replaces or makes deletable. (2) Try, in order: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect. (3) Treat every [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
DATE: 2026-11-06 — owner statements, quoted above.

## Owner rulings 2026-11-06 (second) — OR-1c, the identity lens ALL, and the type of a government report

Given in this session (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMkXnQsEwzR9oaTqn1), in reply to the first three questions of the owner-decision sheet in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch-2/resolution-analysis-GAP-074-096.md` (section B), and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Each answer is quoted verbatim, including its lower case:

1. OR-1c: "link table unless that is more prone to errors"
2. The lens for a clause under a disability heading: "ALL is a generic? what do you even mean? ALL implies it is just good design, not that it is accessible design in particular as it doesn't map to a particular group. I guess we can see it as a universal?"
3. The type of a government report: "if government report is academically sound then it can be t3 I think"

The owner then asked that every fix be queued for a later session, and that the work be committed, merged and closed.

**What this does.** The readings are the assistant's and are marked; the owner's words above are the ruling.

1. **OR-1c.** A link table: a figure is written once and a separate table lists the combinations of codes it concerns. The owner's condition was that the link table not be more error-prone. The assistant measured the alternative: one row per identity and ICF combination would turn the identity-tagged figure rows into many more rows each repeating the same value and quote (`python3 -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);m=dict(c.execute('select identity_code,count(*) from identity_icf_map group by 1'));r=c.execute('select identity_code,count(*) from source_value_extractions where identity_code is not null group by 1').fetchall();print(sum(n for i,n in r),sum(n*max(1,m.get(i,1)) for i,n in r))"`; measured 2026-11-06: 212 rows become 1608 on identity and ICF alone, before access needs). The link table's own error, an orphan link row, is already caught at apply time, because `scripts/migrate_db.py` snapshots `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` before and after a migration and fails on a new violation. [ASSUMPTION: that measurement settles the owner's condition; if the owner reads it otherwise, OR-1c reopens.] The shape of the table, and what happens to the four lens columns already on a figure (a column a committed data migration inserts can never be dropped, so retire writer, then reader, then NULL forward), are the tooling PR's.
2. **The lens ALL.** `ALL` in this project is a scope marker, not a population: `governance/population-taxonomy.md` section 1.3 says it "means this specification applies to all populations", for example Universal Mode code compliance values and universal design principles, and the database describes it as "Item is not population-specific; applies to everyone". The owner reads it as a universal, good design for everyone, which names no particular group and so is not accessible design in particular. [ASSUMPTION: this is read as: a provision written as accessible design, from an accessibility code or a study of disabled people, is not tagged ALL merely because its sentence names no group; it carries the group or groups it serves, and ALL is kept for provisions that are universal good design. The owner hedged ("I guess"), so this is not a final ruling on MOB against ALL for a clause under a disability heading, and one question stands: confirm the reading.] If the reading holds, the sentence of `governance/population-taxonomy.md` section 1.3 naming "code compliance values (e.g., minimum corridor width per code)" as a typical use of ALL is overtaken; no `SUPERSEDES` pair is written because the answer is hedged. Which group a provision carries is judgment's output, filled with the link table of item 1, where one figure can carry several groups. OR-1b is unchanged: a figure tagged ALL reaches only an ALL determination.
3. **A government report.** A government report that is academically sound may be tier 3. [ASSUMPTION: "t3" is tier 3; "academically sound" is the test OR-5 already uses for a Co-1 source; the answer takes the option "stay `grey`, tier 3" and rejects reclassifying to `clinical` and a new route to tier 1.] REF-00468, REF-01005 and REF-01008 stay as filed. The line of `governance/tier-system.md` that lists `grey` as "occasionally" tier 1 for unpublished primary research is the text this answer leaves in tension; correcting it is queued as a doctrine change and not made here. Whether a given report is academically sound is judged per source and is not decided by this entry.

**What is unblocked, and what still waits.** OR-1c is answered, so the lens-routing change (T-3) and the tagging of existing rows (D-2) can be designed, as a tooling pull request first. The tier of REF-00468 is settled as filed. Waiting on the owner: the confirmation in item 2, and the five other questions of the sheet (the term for a width at a turn, sub-national instruments, adversarial pass 7, a library route for six papers and BS 8300, in-place correction of a locator).

CONDITION: any session designing the lens-routing change or filling lenses on figures (T-3, D-2), writing a lens on a figure from an accessibility code or a study of disabled people, or typing a government report.
ACTION: (1) Carry several codes of one model on a figure by a link table; do not write the figure once per combination. (2) Do not tag a provision from an accessibility code ALL because its sentence names no group; leave the tag to the lens fill and treat ALL as a universal-design marker, until the owner confirms or corrects item 2. (3) Keep `grey` government reports that are academically sound at tier 3; do not reclassify them to `clinical`. (4) Treat every [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
DATE: 2026-11-06 — owner statements, quoted above.

## Owner statements 2026-11-06 — the old item subjects are admitted as a basis for the base vocabulary; the base must serve every P1+P2+P3 language; Opus plans the population

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iPbFEPovMCoes1oKx9 after a read-only review of the base tables (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/base-review.md`, PR #213), and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim; the first two arrived mid-turn.

On language and jurisdiction scope:

> "these base tables, as per our aliases and native terms and translations and multilingual and multijurisdictional requirements etc, must work across all languages that we have defined for this current edition of project (the p1+2+3, I think it's called, for the initial countries to focus on)"

On prior work:

> "we should have some work already done based upon previous editions of this project and those listed specification items"

On the question the review put (whether the 93 item subjects, value-stripped, may be admitted as a catalogue for prepopulating parameter names, overriding the 2026-10-09 exclusion):

> "great work. yes, use the 93 items with stripped values as a basis. with your criticisms in mind, have Opus plan out a strategy with which to populate the base tables and address all listed issues such that we have a truly comprehensive international project without English bias"

**What this establishes**

1. **The 93 item subjects are admitted as a basis.** This reverses, for the pre-reset `items` names only, the 2026-10-09 clause that the old Part 4 item names "are not a permitted source" (the entry "Owner statements 2026-10-09 — every source is scanned for every parameter…", item 3). The mark of that supersession is this item: the back-pointer grammar cannot mark a clause that sits in this ledger.
2. **What "basis" does not do.** It does not mint anything. The guard the owner chose on 2026-10-09 stands: "Screen, then you approve". Each candidate is screened (no digit, comparator or min/max word, no old item code, not already held) and listed in one table with the item it came from, and the owner approves that table in a further dated entry before any term is minted. [ASSUMPTION: "use … as a basis" means a source of candidate names under that guard, not an approval of the names, and not a licence to file findings into the old item containers. The deletion of the item layer (2026-09-01) stands; an item subject is a lead for a quantity, never a container.]
3. **A route is owed.** `terms.catalogue`'s CHECK already admits the pre-reset corpus file, but `_resolve_catalogue_entry` resolves it for `terms:<TERM-ID>` only. Admitting the item subjects needs a resolver and no schema change, and it ships as a tooling-only pull request before any name is minted (`CLAUDE.md` rule 10).
4. **The language scope is P1+P2+P3.** The base tables, aliases, native terms and translations must work across every language those jurisdictions require. [ASSUMPTION: the set is the one recorded in `workplan/2026-10-30-ramp-spec-pages/HANDOFF.md` section 3 (US UK AU CA DE NO SE ISO EU; FR CH NL DK FI BE IE ES IT PT; JP SG NZ KR CN), which the owner confirmed on 2026-10-30 ("Yes it is P1+P2+P3"), giving the 14 languages `lang_jur_map` pairs with them. The 2026-10-29 OR-12a scoping-out of Arabic, Bengali, Hindi and Swahili is not touched by this statement.]
5. **Opus plans.** An Opus-class planner writes a strategy to populate the base tables and to address the review's listed issues (the parameter list at ten rows, the unverified and English-biased alias layer, the English-only ICF, identity, need and room tables, the empty medical lens, the missing topics). The plan is a proposal: it approves nothing and writes no rows.

CONDITION: any session asking whether the 93 old item names may seed parameters, whether item subjects are still excluded as a source, whether the base vocabulary must cover the P1+P2+P3 languages, or who plans the population of the base tables.
ACTION: (1) Treat the pre-reset item subjects, value-stripped and with their codes removed, as a permitted source of candidate names, never as containers. (2) Mint no name from them before a tooling pull request adds the catalogue route and the owner approves the screened table in a dated entry. (3) Build base vocabulary, aliases and native terms for every P1+P2+P3 language, with in-language provenance (R11); never treat an English term translated word for word as a native term. (4) Treat every [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
DATE: 2026-11-06 — owner statements, quoted above.

## Owner statement 2026-11-06 (second) — every recommendation of the base-population plan is applied

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iPbFEPovMCoes1oKx9, in reply to the plan `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/base-population-plan.md` and its section E of twelve owner decisions, and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. The whole message:

> "apply all recommendations, carefully infer and apply all solutions from my rulings and context required for pipeline to operate, etc"

and, in a message that arrived while the first was being worked on:

> "e1 e3 e4; Appy yes"

[ASSUMPTION: "Appy" is "Apply". The second message names the three items that block the first tooling pull request, E1, E3 and E4, and says yes to each; it is read as confirming their recommended options specifically, so those three do not rest on the blanket reading below.]

**What this decides.** Each decision of the plan's section E is answered by the option the plan marked as recommended, as the plan words it. [ASSUMPTION: a blanket "apply all recommendations" is read as choosing the recommended option of every E-item other than E1, E3 and E4 (which the second message names), including the three of those the plan marks DG-NON (E5 licensing, E6 population taxonomy, E7 jurisdiction), because the owner is the one who decides those and has now decided. It is not read as approving the screened table of item subjects, the mints, the declinations or the stakes table themselves: each of those is a table the owner has not yet seen, and the 2026-10-09 guard ("Screen, then you approve") and the plan's E9 still require the owner's approval of the table before any row is written.]

| Item | Answer applied |
|---|---|
| E1 (DG-NON) | A concept first met outside English is named by the instrument's own phrase, in its own language, until an English-language instrument of a P1+P2+P3 jurisdiction is observed naming the same concept. No English gloss is typed (OR-17). |

TERM-091 (parameter 12) is among the four the plan names; its rename needs the owner's quote on that parameter and is not applied here. |

| E4 (OR-17b) | The model-generated and unrecorded aliases stay as flagged search aids, never vocabulary, and are not deleted; each becomes vocabulary only when an instrument in its language is read and the phrase is found there. |

**What it asks of the pipeline.** "Apply … context required for pipeline to operate" is read as: build the tooling the plan names (its T1 to T4) in a tooling-only change before any row is written (`CLAUDE.md` rule 10), keep the ledger and the instrument consistent with the answers above, and stage the research that follows. CONDITION: any session asking how a concept first met in a non-English instrument is named, whether the unattested aliases are vocabulary or may be deleted, whether item subjects are pointed at by code or by row, whether WHO titles in other languages may be stored verbatim, whether identity labels in other languages may be recorded, whether Norwegian is split, whether rooms are populated, whether the P1+P2+P3 language-and-jurisdiction pairs are approved bucket members, or whether the axis and method terms are parameters.

(9) Write no row from the item subjects, the stakes proposal or the renames until the owner approves the table in a dated entry. (10) Treat every [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.

## Owner statements 2026-11-06 (third) — the register is written in English first, then translated to search each language; it must not be English-biased

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iPbFEPovMCoes1oKx9 while the RHFAC Rating Survey v4.0 and the CSA/ASC B651 listing were being catalogued, and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim; times in session order.

> "we have categories according to the kind of technique (acoustic, circulation, etc) as well as categories according to building typology and room"

> "and these cross-pollinate each other"

> "what appears in a category specification for type (eg circulation, acoustics) will appear in building typologies and rooms and vice versa"

> "you don't need French edition here"

> "what I mean is that you will build out a comprehensive register of concepts/items/terms/techniques but you have to ensure that you research them across all of our chosen jurisdictions and languages without an English bias"

> "so we are doing prep work to get this all written out in English and then we have to translate it all properly into other languages to search them too"

and, replying to the session's reading of those statements (that a translation is a flagged search seed, and the register also takes concepts from native-language readings):

> "yes"

> "we set up the base and in turn we set up the research coverage"

[ASSUMPTION: "yes" answers the session's reading in point 3 and 4 below; "we set up the base and in turn we set up the research coverage" is read as: the base register is the list the research coverage is derived from, concept by language-and-jurisdiction pair, and coverage is never kept as a second list.]

**What this establishes**

1. **Two category axes that derive from one set of rows.** A technique category (acoustic, circulation …) and a building typology or room are two views of the same criteria. # Catalogue: RHFAC Rating Survey v4.0 and the CSA/ASC B651 listing, as a basis for the base register

Session `session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review`. **A lead catalogue, not evidence and not a specification.** Nothing here is admitted, no database row is written, and every figure below is computed by `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/tools/doc.py` from the persisted survey text (re-run, do not trust the prose). Governing statements: the three 2026-11-06 owner entries in `references/project-standards.md` (the third is this task's).

## 0. How to read this

- **Guideline in approach, not exacting.** The RHFAC survey is a Canadian rating instrument: it lists criteria and weights them by points. It states **no dimension, force, slope or time**. Those live in the codes it rates against (CSA/ASC B651, the National Building Code of Canada and provincial codes), so this catalogue yields concepts and techniques to search for, never values to adopt. A criterion's point weight is RHF's weighting, not a finding about importance for disabled people.
- **English first is preparation, not the register.** The text below is Canadian English from one jurisdiction (CA), one programme and one author. It is the search plan for the other 13 languages of P1+P2+P3 and a seed for the reverse path: concepts that English does not name are added from native-language readings, by the instrument's own phrase (owner E1).
- **Two category axes, one table.** Every criterion carries technique tags and sits in a section that is a room, element or building typology. Both views in section 3 are generated from `rhfac-criteria.tsv`; neither is kept by hand. The technique tags are rule-assigned from the criterion's own words (regexes in `tools/build.py`): a lead for review, with multiple tags allowed because categories overlap by design.

## 1. Sources and what was and was not read

| Source | Retrieved | Read | Not read |
|---|---|---|---|
| RHFAC Rating Survey v4.0 (September 2024), `rickhansen.com/sites/default/files/downloads/2024-10/rhfacratingsurveyv40sept20244r.pdf`, 66 pages, sha256 `94f80b1b6677…` | `retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/94f80b1b66776c72.pdf` | In full, as text (`pdftotext -layout`): every criterion title and point weight; the prerequisites; the certification levels. | Page images, if any carry content the text layer lacks. The survey names no figures, so the loss is judged small, **[UNVERIFIED]**. |
| CSA/ASC B651:23 (January 2023, revised June 2025), 283 pages, supplied by the owner as a Google Drive file `1_mvami5rXIBzyBNOZ7fR-blAp42GAUb8`, sha256 `4fae63595a10…`; the first two attempts returned Google's sign-in page, the retry after the owner changed the sharing returned the PDF | `4fae63595a101516.pdf` (committed in the retrieval log under the owner's fourth 2026-11-06 ruling) | **By headers only:** table of contents, defined-term names, clause 1.6, headings and opening lines of 4.7, headings of Annexes A to F (section 2.4). | **The body clauses and every figure, table and value. [SKIPPED: B651:23 body text — by instruction (read by headers); not read.]** The publisher's own direct URL (`csagroup.org/wp-content/uploads/2430328-1.pdf`) returned a Cloudflare 403 and has no Wayback snapshot; no block-evasion was attempted. |
| ASC database listing for CSA/ASC B651, `accessible.canada.ca/…/csa-asc-b651-accessible-design-built-environment`, sha256 `b0ca9f638851…` | `b0ca9f6388515ded.html` | The listing page: a scope paragraph and five change headings. | Nothing further; it is a summary page. |
| CSA Group store page for CSA/ASC B651:23, `csagroup.org/store/product/csa-asc%20b651%3a23/`, sha256 `a038f0903154…` | `a038f09031540a36.html` | Edition history (1990, 1995, 2004, 2012, 2018 withdrawn; 2023 current), languages (English, French), and a nine-item list of changes in the 2023 edition (anthropometric dimensions, interpretation notes, luminance contrast, tactile direction indicator positioning, functional and cognitive barriers, power-assisted door controls, platform-lift minimum size, water-bottle filling stations, water-fountain controls). | The standard. |

The French RHFAC survey and guide and the French ASC page were retrieved before the owner said they are not needed here; they are in the retrieval log and nothing is drawn from them.

**Parse integrity (computed):** 640 criteria across 74 sections in 12 chapters; 70 stated section totals read, 70 sections with criteria summed (chapter 12 scored differently); mismatches (section, sum of the criterion points, the total the survey states): [('8.12', 17, 19), ('8.13', 22, 24)]. A mismatch is the SURVEY's own arithmetic, kept as printed: the criteria were re-read against the text and none was dropped.

## 2. The register this seeds

The base holds 94 terms and 10 active parameters (`select count(*) from terms`; `… from base_parameters where status='active'`). The 640 criteria collapse to 430 distinct normalised statements, of which 32 recur in three or more sections. Those recurring statements are the technique concepts that every typology shares; the long tail is typology-specific. Rows for the register are written only after the tooling PR merges (CLAUDE.md rule 10).

### 2.1 Concepts recurring in three or more sections (the shared technique vocabulary)

### 2.2 Criteria that name something measurable (quantity-bearing words)

The survey gives no values, but its words name the quantities a code would set. Word → number of sections whose criteria use it (regex `QB` in `tools/doc.py`; a lead for the open pass, not a parameter list).

### 2.4 CSA/ASC B651:23, digested by headers

**Read by headers only** (owner instruction): the table of contents, the 58 defined-term names of clause 3.1, clause 1.6 (the shall/should/may convention), the three headings and opening lines of 4.7 (functional and cognitive barriers; environmental intolerances; acoustics), and the headings of Annexes A to F. The standard's body clauses were not read, so **no dimension, force, slope or time is recorded here** and none should be inferred. Full heading list with pages: `b651-headings.tsv` (232 headings, generated by `tools/b651.py`).

**Document facts (title page and revision block):** CSA/ASC B651:23, National Standard of Canada, 'Accessible design for the built environment', January 2023, REVISED JUNE 2025 (errata to clause 5.2.2, Tables 8 a) to d) and Figures 20 a) to d); earlier errata of July 2023 to clauses 1.4, 5.5.1, 6.8.2, 9.4.1 and A.10); 283 pages; English and French editions exist; developed under Accessibility Standards Canada with a technical committee that includes persons with disabilities; the document says it focuses on national and international best practice 'as opposed to focusing on minimum technical requirements'; clause 1.6 separates requirement, recommendation and option by 'shall', 'should' and 'may', and Annexes A to F are informative.

**Legal notice and the owner's ruling:** the PDF's notice says users may not 'make an electronic copy of this document'. The owner ruled on 2026-11-06 (fourth entry, `references/project-standards.md`) that the project, a not-for-profit volunteer advocacy project, may hold retrieved standards in the repository, so the PDF is persisted in the retrieval log like any other source. That covers holding it for verification; republishing or rendering its text in the book is a separate question.

### B651 defined terms (names as the standard writes them; Canadian English)

## 4. Beyond these two sources (leads, each [UNVERIFIED] until a source in hand states it)

- **Named by the B651 listing but not by RHFAC:** luminance (colour) contrast as a method; tactile direction indicator positioning; platform size for platform lifts; controls and sizes of power-assisted doors; water-bottle filling stations and fountain controls; anthropometric dimensions as the basis of clearances; functional and cognitive barriers as a category.
- **Categories the survey scores thinly or not at all**, from the project's own vocabulary and ICF frame: sound insulation between spaces and plant noise as measured quantities; vibration; air quality and ventilation (the survey asks only that scents be absent or contained); thermal setpoints; flicker and photosensitive thresholds (the survey asks for none identified); wayfinding for people who are Deafblind; sign-language and captioning provision as a space requirement; evacuation for people who cannot use stairs beyond "area of refuge" and "evacuation chair"; bariatric and short or tall stature ranges (owner-ruled body-size frame, access need A-SIZE); tactile and haptic communication zones; ceiling hoists; adult changing facilities beyond the washroom item; queuing and timed access.
- **Not in either source:** building typologies the survey does not frame (transit stations and vehicles, hospitals and clinics, schools beyond "specialized learning spaces", prisons, places of worship, cemeteries, temporary event structures). Whether a P1+P2+P3 instrument frames them is a question for the native-language readings, not for this list.

## 5. Research coverage, derived from the base

**Principle (owner, 2026-11-06): the base sets the research coverage.** Coverage is one measure of a (concept × language-and-jurisdiction pair) cell, computed from the base and the reading records; no separate list of what has been searched is kept (rules 5 and 8). The pairs are `lang_jur_map` rows for the P1+P2+P3 jurisdictions:

39 pairs (`select language, jurisdiction from lang_jur_map where jurisdiction in (…P1+P2+P3…)`): EN/AU, DE/BE, FR/BE, NL/BE, EN/CA, FR/CA, DE/CH, FR/CH, IT/CH, ZH/CN, DE/DE, DA/DK, ES/ES, DA/EU, DE/EU, EN/EU, ES/EU, FI/EU, FR/EU, IT/EU, NL/EU, PT/EU, SV/EU, FI/FI, SV/FI, FR/FR, EN/IE, IT/IT, JA/JP, KO/KR, NL/NL, NO/NO, EN/NZ, PT/PT, SV/SE, EN/SG, ZH/SG, EN/UK, EN/US.

**Today:** the reading ledger (`v_scan_ledger`) holds, for the 10 active parameters only: NOT-READ 417, EXTRACTED 94, READ-PARTIAL 40, READ-NOTHING-FOUND 22, STATED-ABSENT 7. Not one of the 32 recurring concepts above and none of the long tail has a cell, because none is a term yet; and the language half of a pair cannot be derived for any source, since `evidence_sources.language` is NULL on every row (plan defect A6). **Coverage of the new register is 0 until the first native-language reading is recorded.**

**Cell states** (proposed; the bucket table T-6b is the home): NOT-SEARCHED; SEARCHED-FOUND (phrase, locator, quote, instrument); SEARCHED-ABSENT (the instrument was read in full and states nothing); SEARCHED-QUERY-FAILED (the search shape failed, R14); NOT-OBTAINABLE (instrument held back by paywall or block, with the attempt logged).

## 6. The terminology research pass

This is research, and it needs passes that read instruments in their own language. One pass per language-and-jurisdiction pair:

1. **Instrument list** for the pair: the primary accessibility instrument(s) in force, current editions only (workplan HANDOFF section 3), from `research_code_leads`, `references/standards-registry.md` and what is held. Retrieve each through `retrieval_log.fetch`; a block goes to the Wayback `if_` route (CLAUDE.md section 7); a failure is logged, not hidden.
2. **Search seeds.** The English register is rendered into the language as **flagged, model-generated search seeds** (owner OR-12b, third 2026-11-06 statement): terms the model believes are in use in that jurisdiction, never word for word, recorded as seeds and never as aliases. Seeds only point the reading.
3. **Read the instrument in full in its own language** (OR-13 open pass), not only for the seeds. For each concept found: the phrase **as the instrument writes it**, locator, a verbatim quote that verifies in the saved text, and the instrument. For each concept the instrument treats that the register lacks: the same record, in the instrument's phrase (reverse harvest, E1). For each register concept not found after a full reading: SEARCHED-ABSENT.
4. **Observe → adjudicate → attest** with the verbs that exist (`observe-term`, `adjudicate-term`, `add-alias` or `add-term --from-observation`); a seed whose phrase is found becomes an attested alias in place (migration 117). Rows ship in a research PR after the tooling PR merges.
5. **No pair is second-read before every pair is first-read**, so English does not become the frame (plan C.3).

## 7. What this needs from the owner

## B. Population design, per table

Principles applied to every row of the table below:

- **No row in language X is derived from a row in English.** Every non-English label or alias points at an in-language
  artefact (an observation whose quote verifies in a saved file, or a persisted payload). English is one language among 14
  and gets the same pointer requirement for its jurisdiction variants.
- **Language and jurisdiction are read, not typed** (rule 8): from the observation and its source, as `add-alias` already does.
- **No language CHECK is added.** The language vocabulary is `lang_jur_map`, so a language admitted later is a row, not a migration.

| Table | Target end-state | Single source of truth | Derived, not curated | Pointer | Writer (existing verb, or gap) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `terms` | Every concept any P1-3 instrument treats as a design quantity, element, method or setting, each with provenance: an origin observation (NAMES-NEW) or an approved catalogue entry | the origin observation, or the catalogue entry plus approval heading | The label's language: from the origin observation; `en` for a catalogue mint | `term_adjudications` → `observed_terms` → `evidence_sources` | `add-term --from-observation`; `mint-term-from-catalogue`. **Gap T2:** bind the name to the observed phrase |
| `base_parameters` | Every term that names a quantity under determination; every other term declined with a reason | `terms` + the promotion or declination | Nothing curated; status from verbs | `term_id` (UNIQUE) | `add-parameter`, `decline-parameter`, `merge-parameter`, `set-parameter-direction` |
| `term_aliases` | For each term and each P1-3 pair: the phrase that jurisdiction's own instrument uses, attested; model-generated rows held as flagged search aids only | `observed_terms` row (phrase, language, locator, quote) | alias text, language, jurisdiction: read from the observation and source | **Gap T3:** a nullable `observation_id` foreign key | `add-alias`; **gap T3:** attach a pointer to an already-held alias instead of refusing |
| `base_icf` | Every code a held need, identity or parameter crosses to, plus chapters d4, d5, e1, e2, e3, e4, e5 as a completeness frame; English title from WHO bytes | persisted WHO payload | title verified as a substring of the payload | `title_source = payload:<file>` | `add-icf-code`, `set-icf-title --title-payload`; **gap T4:** replace a non-payload title with a payload-verified one, recording the old |
| Labels in other languages (ICF titles, identity, need, room, medical display names) | One label per code per language (and per jurisdiction where usage differs), each pointing at its in-language artefact | the artefact | language, jurisdiction from the artefact | **Proposed T5:** one table, five nullable foreign keys (identity, need, ICF, medical, room), CHECK exactly one, mirroring the ruled four-lens-column shape (ledger, 2026-08-28 lens ruling as amended by D-0182) | none today; T5 waits on owner decisions E5, E6, E8 |
| `base_taxonomy_identity` | Unchanged (DG-NON). Labels per language through T5 | owner rulings | — | — | none, deliberately |
| `access_needs` / `access_need_icf` | Stakes assigned with warrant; ICF crossings `confirmed` only against WHO bytes | owner-approved table for stakes | stakes vocabulary from the column CHECK; retire `access_stakes` if nothing reads it (§8) | `access_need_icf` | **[GAP]** no verb found for `typical_stakes`; confirm with `grep -n 'typical_stakes' scripts/db.py` before planning one |
| `base_taxonomy_medical` + maps | The correspondence set the 2026-09-11 correction bounds, then on demand | WHO ICD-11 release file, persisted | anchors verified from bytes (`icd11_verified_at`) | crossings to identity and ICF | `add-medical --icd11-payload` |
| `rooms` | Frozen until a reader exists (E8) | — | — | none points at it | none needed |
| `lang_jur_map` | The 39 P1-3 pairs (D15) approved as bucket members; varieties per E7 | owner approval per row (T-6b) | — | bucket table points at pairs (OR-8) | T-6b, already ruled; not new here |

### B.1 How a concept that originates in a non-English source becomes a term

| Option | What it does | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A (recommended).** The term's label is the source's own phrase, in its own language; `canonical_en` holds it verbatim; the label's language is derived from the NAMES-NEW observation | No schema change. `add-term` gains one refusal: the name must occur, case-folded, in the observation's `surface_form` (T2). An English name is added only when an English-language instrument of a P1-3 jurisdiction is observed naming the same concept; then `rename-term --from-observation` | Satisfies OR-17 and R11 at once; English loses its privilege; the reader sees the concept as the instrument names it | The column name lies; every reader that renders `canonical_en` must show the label's language. `rename-term` turns the old name into a DEPRECATED alias, which is wrong for a native label: T2 must make it a live SYNONYM in its own language instead |
| B. Rebuild `terms` with `canonical_en` nullable, plus a derived per-language label view | Honest column semantics | Clean model | A table rebuild against every reader (`grep -c canonical_en scripts/db.py`) and the views that name it; net code grows; no ruling needs it yet |
| C. A typed English gloss | — | — | Forbidden by OR-17; listed only to reject |

The definition and scope note may describe the concept in English prose, because prose is ours (the 2026-09-11 reasoning,
"identifiers are facts while prose is ours"); a name may not be invented. Remediation of D8 and D9: flag the four terms now; correct
each in a data PR by `rename-term` to the observed phrase, on the owner's word for the parameter among them (TERM-091 is parameter 12).

### B.2 Native term versus translation

- **Rule.** An attested alias is a phrase a jurisdiction's own instrument uses, observed in that instrument in its own language.
  It is typed SYNONYM, NARROWER or BROADER, never TRANSLATION (T3 refuses TRANSLATION on an attested alias). An officially
  published English version of a non-English instrument is a translation: its phrases are observed with the language they appear
  in, but they attest the English-language usage of nobody's jurisdiction and are excluded from `add-alias` for an EN alias unless
  the instrument is authoritative in English in that jurisdiction (T3 refuses where the alias language is not paired with the
  source's jurisdiction in `lang_jur_map`).
- **Jurisdiction tagging** is the source's jurisdiction, read by `add-alias`. That already separates DE/AT/CH German, FR/BE/CH/CA
  French, NL/BE Dutch, PT usage, and US/UK/AU/CA/IE/NZ/SG English. It does not separate two written standards inside one
  jurisdiction (Norwegian Bokmål and Nynorsk) or scripts (Chinese), which is E7.
- **Legal designations** (a JA, KO or ZH statutory term of art) are terms in their own right under B.1, not aliases of an English
  concept, wherever the instrument defines them.

### B.3 Verifying the 880 unrecorded and 1163 model-generated aliases

Status meanwhile: **usable only as flagged search aids** (OR-12b), **never vocabulary** (OR-17), pending the owner's OR-17b (E4).
The route is not a separate glossary-verification protocol but the ordinary evidence path, which removes the need for
`VERIFIED-GLOSSARY` as a hand marker (rule 8):

1. Per language, the glossary is the P1-3 instrument's own definitions clause, or a national standards body's terminology
   standard, admitted as a source (`add-source`), its text persisted with `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py` `fetch()` and
   registered with `scripts/research/full_text.py`. Wayback `if_` fallback per CLAUDE.md section 7 for a block.
2. Each phrase found is `observe-term`'d with locator and verbatim quote, `adjudicate-term`'d NAMES-EXISTING, then `add-alias`.
   With T3, a held model-generated alias whose text matches gains the pointer in place and becomes attested; an attested phrase
   not held becomes a new row.
3. A model-generated alias the instrument contradicts, or never uses after a full open pass of that pair, stays flagged; whether it
   is deleted is E4. No alias is ever generated to fill a gap (OR-17).

Order: one language at a time, the instrument with the largest definitions section first. `alias_provenance_audit` reports
progress per language; it must classify from the pointer (T3), or it measures text, not attestation.

### B.4 ICF and ICD-11 titles in each language

- **English titles first**, from a WHO ICF payload persisted under `retrieval-log/`, through `set-icf-title --title-payload`; T4
  replaces the 29 non-payload titles. Before T4 ships, confirm the payload check anchors the title to its code, not just anywhere in
  the file ([GAP]: `set_icf_title` tests `title in body`, a substring match a neighbouring code's title can satisfy).
- **Other languages** go to the T5 label table, each label pointing at a persisted WHO or national-body payload in that language.
  Which of the 14 languages WHO or national bodies publish for ICF and for ICD-11 is **[UNVERIFIED]**; measure by retrieval, never
  by recollection. The ICD-11 English release file is already held (`ls retrieval-log/session_2026-09-11-medical-lens-icd11`).
- **Is a translation table a second home?** No, if it holds only non-derivable facts: WHO's published title in language X is a
  different fact from its English title, keyed on the same code (a pointer, rule 5). It becomes a second home if it also holds the
  English title already in `base_icf.title`; T5 therefore refuses an English row for a code that `base_icf` titles. Whether the
  titles may be stored verbatim under the guidebook's licence is E5 (DG-NON, licensing).

### B.5 Identity, access-need, room and stakes labels

- Identity codes and English display names are untouched (DG-NON). A label in language X is the community's own designation,
  attested in an in-language Co-1 source of a P1-3 jurisdiction, never a translation of the English display name. Where communities
  in one language differ (identity-first versus person-first), the label carries its jurisdiction; where no attestation exists the
  code has no label in X and the gap is visible. Mechanism and certifier are E6.
- Need labels and medical display names are our prose; a non-English rendering is a translation of our prose, which R11 does not
  forbid for prose but must be marked as ours. Defer until a reader in that language exists (no render work is in scope).
- Rooms: frozen (E8). Stakes: one owner-approved table (E9).

### B.6 The medical lens

Populate, in this order: (1) the correspondence set under the 2026-09-11 CORRECTION entry, from the identity registry and the
functional-axis terms, excluding the identity-first and umbrella codes that entry and `governance/functional-taxonomy.md` name;
anchor on the block whose title states the presentation; every anchor verified against the persisted release file through
`add-medical --icd11-payload`; (2) then on demand from admitted sources. Leave empty: entity-level codes, any chapter mirror, and
any row whose anchor cannot be verified from bytes (`icd11_verified_at` stays NULL and the row is not written). Medical display
names are our prose (the `insert_medical` docstring). This is Opus-class judgment (pruning the derived join, per the 2026-09-11
ruling) and its own research PR.

## C. Route to a comprehensive parameter list

### C.1 The screened catalogue of item subjects (route i)

A read-only subcommand (T1) prints one table for the owner. It never writes the database. Per row:

| Column | Filled by | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| pointer | machine | `items:<rowid>` into the pre-reset database; the old code is not shown (the 2026-11-06 ruling: "with their codes removed") |
| stripped name | machine | parentheticals and bracketed text removed; then `_VALUE_BEARING` and `_ITEM_CODE` re-tested (imported, not retyped) |
| still value-bearing | machine | D22 → 2 of 93 after stripping (2026-11-06) |
| prescription-bearing | judgment | condition clauses the regex cannot see (DR-2026-08-19 section 1.1 counted names carrying prescriptive conditions); a yes means reject or reword from a source, never mint |
| nearest held term | machine | `_name_holder` on name and aliases; D22 → 8 exact matches |
| kind | judgment, from `quantity / element / intervention / method / setting / lens` | |
| quantity implied | judgment | **a lead only.** The implied quantity's name is not in the item name, so minting it would be coining; it goes to the open-pass lead list |
| recommendation and reason | judgment | mint as term and promote (quantity); mint as term and decline (element, intervention: `decline-parameter --reason`); hold as lead; reject (held, prescription-bearing, or not ours) |

The owner approves the table in a dated ledger entry; then `mint-term-from-catalogue --catalogue _archived/data/corpus-pre-reset-2026-08-06.db
--entry-ref items:<rowid> --approval-ref "<heading>"` per approved row, followed by `add-parameter` or `decline-parameter`.
An element is a term, never a parameter (OR-14: element pages derive from parameters through a typed pointer). The catalogue
seeds English names only; it decides nothing about whether a concept exists, and every term it mints enters the alias coverage
metric with zero attested pairs.

### C.2 The open pass over held codes (route ii, OR-13 and OR-16)

Held texts are derived, not listed: for each instrument, `grep -l '"<ref_id>"' retrieval-log/*/manifest.jsonl` and
`select * from v_scan_ledger where ref_id = ?`. Most held non-English codes are single clauses retrieved for the ramp work (titles
naming one section, e.g. `select ref_id, original_title from evidence_sources where evidence_type='code'`). So route ii gives
full texts mainly for SG, UK, US and IE; it is the fastest first step and the most English one, which is why C.3 interleaves.
Each reading: `record-scan --mode catalogue --method full-read --text-scope full --open-pass-done`, with every new design quantity
`observe-term`'d verbatim.

### C.3 Native-language open passes over P1-3 instruments (route iii)

1. **Instrument list per pair**, derived from `research_code_leads`, `references/standards-registry.md` and the held codes,
   restricted to current editions (HANDOFF section 3). DK, IT and CN have nothing (D16): their first act is a search for the primary
   instrument, logged per R8.
2. **Order:** one full open pass per pair before any pair's second; within that, free official full texts before paywalled ones
   (availability per instrument is [UNVERIFIED] until fetched); English pairs are not first. A block goes to the Wayback route of
   CLAUDE.md section 7, with its recorded limit (the CSA B651 failure).
3. **Stopping rule, derived.** A pair is exhausted when every current instrument on its list has a full-read, full-scope, open-pass
   scan at the current `catalogue_version`, and the last such round produced no NAMES-NEW and no DEFERRED observation for that pair.
   A new parameter raises the catalogue version and `scan_debt` re-opens targeted readings, so the list closes only at a fixed point
   where a whole round adds nothing. No count is set by hand.

### C.4 Completeness checks from the other direction (route iv)

ICF chapters d4, d5, d6, d9 and e1 to e5 (from the WHO payload), `research_code_leads`, and the standards registries are read as
**checks**, not name sources: for each ICF activity or environmental code, ask whether any parameter's term addresses it; a miss is a
lead for the open pass, recorded as a gap. No ruling permits naming a parameter from ICF text.

### C.5 Coverage metric (OR-8), computed from the database

For each active parameter *p* and each approved bucket member (*L*, *J*):

- **read(p, L, J)**: some current instrument of *J* whose text language is *L* has a `v_scan_ledger` status of EXTRACTED,
  STATED-ABSENT or READ-NOTHING-FOUND for *p*. Needs A6 fixed (source language populated) and T-6b built.
- **named(p, L, J)**: an attested alias (pointer, T3) of *p*'s term in *L* from a source of *J*.

Report both per parameter and per pair, as counts with the command, never as a stored figure. It ships as one view in the T-6b PR,
which already plans `v_coverage_parameter_via_admission`; extend that rather than add a second view.

### C.6 Priority order

1. T1-T4 tooling PR. 2. Screened catalogue table, owner approval, mints and declinations. 3. Decline the non-quantity terms
already held (lens, method, economics and similar, D18) with reasons. 4. Route ii open passes. 5. Route iii, interleaved.
6. Alias attestation (B.3) rides on 4 and 5; nothing is attested separately from a reading. 7. ICF English titles, then labels.
8. Medical correspondence set. 9. Directions (`set-parameter-direction`) for each parameter as it is promoted.

167	## Where Spanish carves the field differently (instrument-derived; glosses ours)
168	1. **A ramp is defined by a slope threshold, and the two orders set it differently.** DB-SUA: "Los itinerarios cuya pendiente exceda del 4% se consideran rampa". RD 505 adds "a nivel" and "entre diferentes niveles". Corridor width is a row of the route definition. "Estrechamientos puntuales" (permitted pinch points) are a sub-quantity the register lacks.
170	3. **Landing is two words for one object.** DB-SUA uses "meseta" and TMA uses "rellano". The ends of a ramp are a "superficie horizontal" or "espacio", not a landing.

174	7. **Accessibility sits inside a safety code.** Headroom (SUA 2), lighting (SUA 4) and slip (SUA 1) are fall and impact *safety* exigencias. SUA 9 holds only provision and signage, and most access geometry is in the anejo A definitions.
175	8. **The rules are organised by use class and by definitions.** The named "Uso" building classes of anejo A, plus "uso restringido", "uso público" and "zonas de ocupación nula", switch rules on and off. 176	9. **Cognitive accessibility has its own national regulation, built on a native frame.** RD 707/2026 art. 7.2 names "Deambulación, Aprehensión, Localización, Comunicación" (DALCO), "Control de los estímulos sensoriales" and three graded text registers: "Lectura fácil", "Lenguaje claro" and "Lenguaje sencillo". By source, `awk -F'\t' 'NR>1{print $2"\t"$3}' $D/coverage.tsv | sort | uniq -c` gave: catalogue 2.1 22/8/2; catalogue 2.2 13/3/2; base parameters 7/1/2; the 15 B651 headings RHFAC does not name 8/1/6.

115	- Held pt aliases in the texts: search-log S12 gave 10 of 114 by substring. 0 aliases are tagged PT, and no parameter-level TRANSLATION alias occurs.

117	## Where Portuguese carves the field differently from English (instrument-derived; glosses ours)
118	1. **Ramp is defined by slope, and run by projection.** "Os troços de percursos pedonais com inclinação igual ou superior a 5 % devem ser considerados rampas" (4.7.6). Run length is "projecção horizontal". Each limit is a triple of inclinação, desnível and projecção horizontal, with "valores interpolados" allowed between triples. A separate relaxed set applies to "obras de alteração ou conservação".
119	2. **"Escadarias em rampa"** (stepped ramp) is its own element with its own "desenvolvimento", and has no register row.
120	3. **Tread is a depth in buildings and a length in the street.** The tread is "profundidade (cobertor)" in 2.4.3, but "Comprimento (cobertor)" in the public-way stair table (1.3.1). Riser is "altura (espelho)". Landings split into "patamares" (ends) and "patins" (intermediate). Ramp landings are "plataformas horizontais de descanso".
121	4. **Turning is two categories.** Manoeuvres are "sem deslocamento" (rotação de 90º/180º/360º) or "com deslocamento" (mudança de direcção de 90º/180º/180º em T). The portaria instead speaks of a "diâmetro das zonas de manobra". There is no single "turning circle".
122	5. **Contrast is not quantified, but floor reflectance is.** It is a recommended band, "reflectância média … entre 15 % e 40 %" (4.7.2). That is a luminance-reflectance quantity without a contrast pair, which LRV contrast (parameter 8) does not capture.
123	6. **Door hardware turns on "maçaneta".** In PT-PT the "puxadores em forma de maçaneta" are forbidden (4.9.9). The held BR seed "maçaneta tipo alavanca" would point a PT search at a prohibited object.
124	7. **Surface properties are defined terms:** Estável, Durável, Firme, Contínua (4.7.1), each with its own definition. Slip resistance appears only as "boa aderência mesmo na presença de humidade ou água" for unenclosed and wet spaces, and as "antiderrapante" for nosing strips and pool surrounds.
125	8. **"espaços encerrados" / "não encerrados"** is a defined split that changes values (headroom 2 m / 2,4 m) and the surface rules.
126	9. **Tiers by use, not by building type.** A toilet tier is triggered by "for previsível um uso frequente" (2.9.4 4), 2.9.6).
127	10. **Existing housing has its own regime (portaria, secondary).** Intervenção simples, média and profunda (N1/N2/N3); "parcela acessível"; "compartimentos essenciais à acessibilidade" by dwelling type (T3); and "medidas de mitigação" vs "medidas de compensação" (equivalent performance) vs "Cumprimento das NTA".
128	11. **Drafting.** The annex mixes "deve" with "É recomendável". Exceptions are an argued route (art. 10: "desproporcionadamente difíceis", heritage case by case, with the justification published). Compliance runs through a "plano de acessibilidades" and a "termo de responsabilidade".

130	## Defects found in the METHOD
131	- D1. **The held source was not the edition in force.** REF-01032 is the 2006 original. Its currency note lists four amending decrees, and the PGDL page also shows Lei 44/2026 (on arts 12 and 21). A pass that read only the held source would have read a superseded annex: 3.3.4 1)–2) are revoked by DL 10/2024.
132	- D2. **The consolidated host omits every table and figure**, so a full read needs two texts of different dates. The labels were checked only where read, and the figure drawings were not seen.
133	- D3. **Substring alias hits over-attest** ("banco" hits banks and worktops). Same as FR D3.
134	- D4. **The language-tag carve is weak.** All 114 pt aliases are BR-tagged or untagged, none PT. BR and PT terms differ in sense here ("maçaneta").
135	- D5. **The 2.2 quantity words remain senses, not concepts** ("volume" = traffic volume; "capacity" = car-park and hall capacity). FOUND-PARTIAL and ABSENT were judged by hand in `PARTIAL`/`ABSENT`.
136	- D6. **The instrument list is not derivable:** `research_code_leads` has no PT row, and the registry entry has no amendment history. Portaria 301/2019 came from web search.
137	- D7. **No locate_quote route for derived PDF text.** The raw-byte check cannot see the 2006 figure labels.
138	
139	## Self-attack: the five likeliest ways this record is wrong
140	1. **The PGDL host is not the official journal.** It may lag or mis-transcribe an amendment, and it was not cross-checked against a DR consolidated text. Lei 44/2026 is taken from its own note.
141	2. **Figure labels come from the 2006 original.** If DL 10/2024 or another amendment changed a table, those labels may be stale. The annex amendment note names only 3.3.4.
142	3. **The portaria rows rest on an aggregator copy.** Quadro 2 is missing, and the wording may differ from the DR original.
143	4. **Sense judgments are mine.** For example: "plataformas horizontais de descanso" read as level landings, "protecções de banheira" as B651 enclosures, "cobertas" as shelter, and "obras nos percursos acessíveis" as scaffolding. Some FOUND or FOUND-PARTIAL calls may be too generous.
144	5. **Absence is scoped to three texts.** Lighting, acoustics, bollards and speed bumps may sit in other PT rules (acoustic regulation, road code, municipal regulations) that were not read. SEARCHED-ABSENT here does not mean absent from Portuguese law.

146	# Pass record: terminology pass ZH/CN (Simplified), session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review
147	
148	**Verdict.** The current national accessibility code, GB 55019-2021 《建筑与市政工程无障碍通用规范》, a fully mandatory code in force since 2022-04-01, was retrieved from gov.cn and read in full. So was the 2023 《中华人民共和国无障碍环境建设法》 (12371.cn, a 新华社 republication). Of 75 register concepts: 47 FOUND, 17 FOUND-PARTIAL, 11 SEARCHED-ABSENT, with 95 reverse-harvest phrases. **Caveat:** the official GB 55019 PDF is image-only. Its "saved text" is my corrected OCR transcription, not the artefact's bytes, so the build verifies its quotes against my transcription. The older and much longer design code, GB 50763-2012 《无障碍设计规范》, is NOT-OBTAINABLE: MOHURD's site is refused at the egress proxy and Wayback holds no snapshot. Every ABSENT result rests on two short texts, and GB 50763 is the likeliest home of most of the missing detail. Nothing was written to the database, committed or pushed.
149	
150	## How the instrument list was built
151	The base gave nothing for China: `research_code_leads` has 0 rows matching CN, and `evidence_sources` has 0 CN rows. `references/standards-registry.md` names only GB 50763-2012 and does not know GB 55019. The list therefore came from web search (search-log W1 to W7). The gov.cn notice (公告2021年第174号) supplied both attachments, and its attachment 2 shows that GB 55019 repealed only five mandatory clauses of GB 50763, so the rest of GB 50763 still stands. Building-specific regulation sits in these engineering codes. The statute sets duties and refers design to 无障碍设施工程建设标准 (arts. 12, 15).
152	
153	## Retrieved and read
154	- GB 55019-2021: 前言, 目次, chapters 1 to 5 (printed pp. 1–17), read in full from the page images. The code has no figures. The PDF has no cover, title or notice page. Transcript `text/ee78b16e1dec13b8.txt`.
155	- The 2023 law, arts. 1–72, read in full (`text/575638778aada9c1.txt`). Attachment 2 (repealed clauses) and the notice were also read (`text/9cffed8f3e412af0.txt`, `text/96574756986c5488.txt`).
156	- Not read: GB 50763-2012 (NOT-OBTAINABLE, above). Also not read, because of the budget: GB 50096 (residential), GB 50624 (handover and maintenance), the road and transit codes, and local standards (Beijing PDFs were seen in search results). Currency after 2021 for GB 55019, and after 2023 for the law, is UNVERIFIED.
157	
158	## Counts (re-run, do not trust; from the repo root, D=scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/terminology-pass/ZH-CN)
159	- Rebuild and verify: `python3 -I $D/build.py`. It reports register 75, observations 79, reverse-harvest 95 and failures 0, and exits 1 on any failure.
160	- Status: `cut -f4 $D/coverage.tsv | tail -n +2 | sort | uniq -c` gives 47 / 17 / 11. By source: `cut -f3,4 $D/coverage.tsv | tail -n +2 | sort | uniq -c` (catalogue 2.1: 22/8/2; 2.2: 13/4/1; parameters: 6/2/2; B651-only headings: 6/3/6).
161	- Distinct phrases: `awk -F'\t' 'NR>1{print $2}' $D/observations.tsv | sort -u | wc -l` gives 77. By instrument: `awk -F'\t' 'NR>1{print $4}' $D/observations.tsv | sort | uniq -c` gives 76 GB 55019 and 3 law. For the reverse harvest it gives 82 and 13.
162	- Raw-byte check: the 16 law quotes all occur in the raw HTML (`retrieval_log.locate_quote`, kind 'unscoped', no ref_id). The GB 55019 quotes cannot be checked against bytes, because no text exists in the PDF.
163	- Held zh aliases found as substrings of the two texts: 17 of 155 (`select distinct alias from term_aliases where lower(language) like 'zh%'`, each tested with `in` against the whitespace-free texts). A hit is presence only: 通道 and 轮椅 hit only inside longer phrases. 走廊宽度, 坡道坡度, 门宽 and 无障碍门槛 (word-for-word translations) occur in neither text.
164	
165	## Where the Chinese code carves the field differently (instrument-derived; glosses ours)
166	1. **Three facility classes, not elements.** Everything is a 无障碍通行设施, a 无障碍服务设施 or a 无障碍信息交流设施 (1.0.3(4)). Information and communication has a whole chapter (ch. 4), which covers phones, kiosks, screen readers, replaceable keyboards and crossing signals. The register has no such axis.
167	2. **One width word, no corridor.** 通行净宽 serves routes, ramps, doors (measured "after opening"), gates and lift doors. 走廊 occurs 0 times. The route object is 无障碍通道 within a continuous 无障碍通行流线 that spans open space, site and building. A crowded-place variant (人员密集的公共场所) raises the width.
168	3. **Two ramps.** The 轮椅坡道 (wheelchair ramp) and the 缘石坡道 (kerb ramp, with its own types: 全宽式单面坡, 三面坡; and parts: 坡口, 过渡空间) are separate objects. A run is bounded by 提升高度 (rise), not by run length, so P12 has no direct counterpart. This matches the Japanese carve.
169	4. **扶手 is both handrail and door handle** (2.5.4(2): 门扇外侧和里侧均应设置扶手，扶手应保证单手握拳操作). The window handle is 执手, and grab bars are 安全抓杆. An English-led seed (把手 for a door handle) would miss the instrument's word. I made exactly that error in transcription before correcting it.
170	5. **Toilet hierarchy.** A 无障碍厕位 (a cubicle inside a public toilet) differs from a 无障碍厕所 (a stand-alone room). Each must allow use by someone 跌倒在地面 (fallen to the floor). The register has one "accessible washroom".
171	6. **Tactile paving is a pair under one parent:** 盲道 = 提示盲道 (warning) + 行进盲道 (guidance), and 2.11.4 requires colour or material difference.
172	7. **Contrast is "colour or brightness" (颜色或亮度对比), never quantified;** for steps it is "colour or material" (颜色或材质). There is no LRV, and no luminance term beyond 亮度.
173	8. **No lighting or acoustics** (照度, 混响, 色温 all 0). Noise appears only as a nuisance of crossing signals (4.0.8(4)).
174	9. **Scoping by user, and the "mainly used by" device.** Stair and handrail rules apply where 视觉障碍者 or 行动障碍者 主要使用. The statutory population is 残疾人、老年人 (law art. 2), with ageing joined by statute (适老化改造, art. 4).
175	10. **Drafting and compliance structure.** The code is "full-text mandatory" (前言), with a performance route for innovation (1.0.4: 论证 against performance), separate lower values for 既有建筑改造或改建, and a relaxation trigger (条件受限). The law adds 替代性措施 where retrofit is infeasible (art. 18), the "five synchronies" (art. 12), and 体验试用 by disabled and older people's representatives (art. 17). **Maintenance is part of the code** (ch. 5: 维护责任人, 应急维护措施).
176	
177	## Defects in the METHOD
178	- **M1. Image-only official texts break the verification chain.** `build.py` proves a quote is in my transcript, not in the artefact. `retrieval_log` has no OCR step and no field marking a text as a transcription, so a reader of observations.tsv cannot tell a transcribed quote from an extracted one except through the text-file header. The method needs a `text_kind` column (extracted / OCR / OCR-corrected) and, ideally, page-image hashes.
179	- **M2. Transcription drift towards the expected word** (把手 for 扶手). This is caught here only because a character diff against raw OCR was run. Any CJK pass that hand-corrects OCR needs that diff as a required step.
180	- **M3. Quantity words of 2.2 are English lemmas.** "level", "distance" and "capacity" map to senses (高差, 距离 as setback, 容纳担架), and FOUND-PARTIAL is assigned by my judgment (the PARTIAL dict), as in the FR pass.
181	- **M4. The register remains criterion-shaped** (C02/C11/C14, C01/C13, C22/C29, C10/C28 are near-duplicates). Here one phrase, 坚固、平整、防滑、不积水, fills three concepts.
182	- **M5. Egress, not the publisher, blocked MOHURD.** That makes GB 50763 NOT-OBTAINABLE from this environment only. A session on another network, or the owner, might reach it. The Wayback route does not help for MOHURD at the paths tried.
183	- **M6. Registry staleness.** `references/standards-registry.md` lists GB 50763 as CURRENT and omits GB 55019 (prevailing since 2022). Not edited (out of scope).
184	
185	## Self-attack: the five likeliest ways this record is wrong
186	1. **Transcription error.** A glyph I misread, or "normalised" as with 把手, would put a wrong phrase into the record and still verify, because the check runs against my own text. 箅子 (grating) is read visually and is the most exposed. Every clause was compared with its page image, but only twice at 300 dpi.
187	2. **ABSENT is narrow.** SEARCHED-ABSENT means absent from GB 55019 and the 2023 law. GB 50763-2012, which is not read, almost certainly treats stair dimensions, outlets, lighting or landscaping somewhere. The 11 ABSENT rows and several PARTIAL rows should be re-run once GB 50763 is in hand.
188	3. **Concept mapping is mine.** Mapping 净高 (low-space barring) to "Height clearance (parkade)", 容纳担架 to "capacity", 临时占用 to "Scaffolding" or 电器 to "Microwave" stretches the senses. The notes flag each one, but the FOUND/PARTIAL status still counts them.
189	4. **Currency and edition.** "In force" rests on the 2021 notice and the statute's commencement article. A later MOHURD amendment notice, or a GB 50763 revision, would not show here. The law's text is a republication (12371/新华社), not the NPC gazette.
190	5. **Locators.** Clause numbers are printed in the code and are reliable. Printed page numbers come from the page footers. Law locators are article numbers counted from the text, and 12371's article breaks were assumed to match the gazette.
191	
192	Files: search-log.md, instruments.tsv, observations.tsv, coverage.tsv, reverse-harvest.tsv, seeds.tsv (10 MODEL-GENERATED), build.py, text/ (four texts), tools/fetch.py.
193

> "this kind of equivalency finding is applicable for all terms researched"

**What this decides.**
1. **The unit of the register is an equivalence class.** A concept has many surface forms per language and jurisdiction. "Accessible parking stall", "handicapped parking", "barrier free parking", "accessibility parking" and "disabled parking" name one concept, and the held instruments add "designated accessible spaces" (RHFAC 1.1) and "designated accessible parking" (CSA/ASC B651:23, clause 9.4).
2. **Non-occurrence in an instrument does not invalidate a form.** Attestation in a code establishes that form as that code's term; it does not decide which other forms are valid equivalents. A form the code does not use is "not attested by these texts", and the sources that could attest it are statutes, road-sign and signage manuals, municipal and advocacy guidance, and ordinary public usage.
3. **Every term researched gets equivalence-class discovery**, not only the first form found. Each form carries its usage type (code term, colloquial, regional variant, outdated or disfavoured, product name) and its attestation (instrument phrase with locator, another source, an owner-supplied form, or an unattested seed). A disfavoured form is recorded with a usage note and not deleted, because people still search with it.
4. **This does not widen what may become vocabulary.** OR-17 and E4 stand: a form enters the base as an attested alias only when a source in its language is read and the phrase is found there. An owner-supplied form is a seed marked as owner-supplied until a source attests it.
